headline: On October 12, 1994: Magellan Spacecraft Burns Up in Venus' Atmosphere
captionCards: Magellan mapped 98% of Venus' surface with radar
Data from Magellan still used in Venus research today
instagramCaption:
The Magellan spacecraft meets its end on Venus.
On October 12, 1994, the Magellan spacecraft, a 1,035-kilogram (2,282 lb) robotic probe launched by NASA, burned up in the atmosphere of Venus. Its mission, which began on May 4, 1989, was to map the surface of Venus using synthetic-aperture radar and measure the planet's gravitational field. The mission provided detailed images and data that have been crucial for understanding Venus. 
Why does this still matter today? It set a new standard for planetary exploration.
